provider.githubToken: Fine-grained personal access token with read-only "Contents" permission.
provider.gitlabToken: Project or group access token with the read_repository scope.
provider.bitbucketToken: Repository, project or workspace access token with the "repository" (read) scope.
provider.azureToken: Personal access token with the Code (Read) scope.
provider.swaggerhubToken: SwaggerHub API key, from your account settings. Public APIs work without one.
provider.githubWebhook: In the repository or organization: Settings > Webhooks > Add webhook. Paste the URL as the payload URL, choose application/json, paste the secret, and pick “Just the push event”.
provider.gitlabWebhook: In the project or group: Settings > Webhooks > Add new webhook. Paste the URL, put the secret in “Secret token”, and tick Push events and Tag push events.
provider.bitbucketWebhook: In the repository: Repository settings > Webhooks > Add webhook. Paste the URL and the secret, and choose the Repository push trigger.
provider.azureWebhook: In the project: Project settings > Service hooks > Create subscription > Web Hooks, trigger “Code pushed”. Paste the URL, use the secret as the basic authentication password (any username), and leave “Resource details to send” on All.

docs.tokenHelp: Sign-in pop-ups (authorization code, implicit, OpenID Connect) can't open inside Confluence, so paste a token from your identity provider here instead. It's added as a Bearer header to requests that don't already have one. It stays in this page's memory only: never saved or logged, and forgotten when you leave. Like all Try it out requests, it goes through SpecPage's backend and only to hosts your admin has approved for Try it out. Client credentials and password flows work from the Authorize button.
